[sources/Is_Sam_Bankman-Fried_a_bad_man_or_a_good_boy_Lawyers_swap_opening_statements_before_first_witnesses_take_the_stand]
The second day of the Sam Bankman-Fried trial featured starkly contrasting opening statements where prosecutors painted him as a liar who stole billions for a lavish lifestyle, while his defense argued he was a good-faith startup founder who acted innovatively and was willing to make customers whole. The proceedings included testimony from a victim, a former friend who admitted to writing code contributing to a crime, and the upcoming appearance of key witnesses like Gary Wang and Matt Huang, setting the stage for the jury to determine the nature of Bankman-Fried's actions.

The second day of the Sam Bankman-Fried trial featured starkly contrasting opening statements where prosecutors painted him as a liar who stole billions for a lavish lifestyle, while his defense argued he was a good-faith startup founder who acted innovatively and was willing to make customers whole. The proceedings included testimony from a victim, a former friend who admitted to writing code contributing to a crime, and the upcoming appearance of key witnesses like Gary Wang and Matt Huang, setting the stage for the jury to determine the nature of Bankman-Fried's actions.

[sources/Is_Sam_Bankman-Fried_a_bad_man_or_a_good_boy_Lawyers_swap_opening_statements_before_first_witnesses_take_the_stand]

- Defense attorneys argued Bankman-Fried acted in good faith, built successful businesses, and did not defraud anyone.
- Witnesses include a victim who lost nearly $100,000, a former friend who admitted to unwittingly writing criminal code, and upcoming star witness Gary Wang.
- The trial highlights the debate over whether Bankman-Fried was a 'man' who lied or a 'boy' who made mistakes in a high-risk startup environment.
- Key figures like Caroline Ellison, Damian Williams, and venture capital partners are expected to provide further insight into the alleged scheme.

- Helena World Chronicle filed a class action antitrust suit against Google and Alphabet in the U.S. District Court in D.C.
- The lawsuit alleges Google uses AI technologies like SGE and Bard to misappropriate publisher content and reduce traffic to news sites.
- Plaintiffs claim Google's actions violate the Sherman Act and Clayton Act, seeking monetary and injunctive relief.
- Reports indicate publishers may lose 20-40% of website traffic when Google's AI products fully roll out.
- Google previously agreed to pay Canadian media $73.5 million annually, but negotiations with Meta remain unresolved.

selected_passages.text:
- The lawsuit was filed in the U.S. District Court in D.C.
- Helena World Chronicle owns two weekly newspapers in Arkansas.
- Google's Knowledge Graph was launched in May 2012.
- By 2020, the Knowledge Graph contained 500 billion facts about 5 billion entities.
- Google drives nearly 40% of The Atlantic's traffic.
- A Wall Street Journal report found AI would answer queries 75% of the time without a click-through.
- Publishers expect to lose 20-40% of website traffic from Google's AI rollout.
- Google links people to publisher websites more than 24 billion times monthly.
- Google paid $73.5 million (100 million Canadian dollars) to Canadian news organizations.
- Meta began blocking news in Canada in August.
- The suit cites a 2023 report from the News Media Alliance regarding AI training data.
- News and Media sites were the third largest category of AI training data according to the Washington Post.
- The Washington Post worked with researchers at the Allen Institute for AI.
- The case references the Epic Games lawsuit against Google over app store antitrust issues.
- The suit asks for an injunction requiring consent to use publisher data for AI training.
- Publishers cannot block SGE because it uses the same web crawler as GoogleBot.
- The law firm handling the case is Hausfeld.
- Google's parent company is Alphabet Inc.
- The suit also references the 2020 Justice Department civil antitrust suit over search advertising.

The second day of the Sam Bankman-Fried trial featured starkly contrasting opening statements where prosecutors painted him as a liar who stole billions for a lavish lifestyle, while his defense argued he was a good-faith startup founder who acted innovatively and was willing to make customers whole. The proceedings included testimony from a victim, a former friend who admitted to writing code contributing to a crime, and the upcoming appearance of key witnesses like Gary Wang and Matt Huang, setting the stage for the jury to determine the nature of Bankman-Fried's actions.

[raw:sources/Is_Sam_Bankman-Fried_a_bad_man_or_a_good_boy_Lawyers_swap_opening_statements_before_first_witnesses_take_the_stand]
Who is Sam Bankman-Fried, the former CEO of crypto exchange FTX? Is he a liar and a fraud? Or did he act in good faith, and like many a startup founder, fly too close to the sun?

[sources/Is_Sam_Bankman-Fried_a_bad_man_or_a_good_boy_Lawyers_swap_opening_statements_before_first_witnesses_take_the_stand]
- Prosecutors alleged Bankman-Fried stole customer funds to finance his lifestyle, political donations, and risky bets through Alameda Research.
- Defense attorneys argued Bankman-Fried acted in good faith, built successful businesses, and did not defraud anyone.
- Witnesses include a victim who lost nearly $100,000, a former friend who admitted to unwittingly writing criminal code, and upcoming star witness Gary Wang.
- The trial highlights the debate over whether Bankman-Fried was a 'man' who lied or a 'boy' who made mistakes in a high-risk startup environment.
- Key figures like Caroline Ellison, Damian Williams, and venture capital partners are expected to provide further insight into the alleged scheme.

[sources/Is_Sam_Bankman-Fried_a_bad_man_or_a_good_boy_Lawyers_swap_opening_statements_before_first_witnesses_take_the_stand]
- Sam Bankman-Fried was the former CEO of FTX.
- The trial took place on the second day with lawyers swapping opening statements.
- Thane Rehn is a prosecutor for the government.
- Mark Cohen is one of Bankman-Fried's lawyers.
- Caroline Ellison is the former CEO of Alameda Research.
- Damian Williams is the U.S. attorney for the Southern District of New York.
- Bankman-Fried's parents are his professorial parents.
- Tom Brady and Larry David are celebrities mentioned in the prosecution's account.
- Alameda Research is a crypto hedge fund owned by Bankman-Fried.
- FTX is a crypto exchange where Bankman-Fried was CEO.
- Marc-Antoine Julliard is a Paris-born cocoa trader who lives in London.
- Julliard tried to pull out almost $100,000 on Nov. 8.
- Adam Yedidia is a fast-talking graduate of MIT.
- Yedidia worked at Jane Street before joining Alameda and FTX.
- Jane Street is a high-frequency trading firm.
- Matt Huang is a former partner at Sequoia Capital.
- Gary Wang is a key Bankman-Fried lieutenant.
- Bankman-Fried spent about seven weeks in a Brooklyn prison.
- The trial was held in New York.
- Court adjourned at 4:30 p.m. on the day of testimony.

- Helena World Chronicle filed a class action antitrust suit against Google and Alphabet in the U.S. District Court in D.C.
- The lawsuit alleges Google uses AI technologies like SGE and Bard to misappropriate publisher content and reduce traffic to news sites.
- Plaintiffs claim Google's actions violate the Sherman Act and Clayton Act, seeking monetary and injunctive relief.
- Reports indicate publishers may lose 20-40% of website traffic when Google's AI products fully roll out.
- Google previously agreed to pay Canadian media $73.5 million annually, but negotiations with Meta remain unresolved.

Who is Sam Bankman-Fried, the former CEO of crypto exchange FTX? Is he a liar and a fraud? Or did he act in good faith, and like many a startup founder, fly too close to the sun?

[entities/sam-bankman-fried]
- From [[sources/Sam_Altman_backs_teens_startup_Google_unveils_the_Pixel_8_and_TikTok_tests_an_ad-free_tier]]: Disgraced entrepreneur accused of orchestrating the collapse of cryptocurrency exchange FTX.
- From [[sources/Is_Sam_Bankman-Fried_a_bad_man_or_a_good_boy_Lawyers_swap_opening_statements_before_first_witnesses_take_the_stand]]: Former CEO of FTX and owner of Alameda Research, central figure in the trial.

[raw:sources/Is_Sam_Bankman-Fried_a_bad_man_or_a_good_boy_Lawyers_swap_opening_statements_before_first_witnesses_take_the_stand]
What the jury will see is a nerdy startup founder who acted in “good faith,” not the prosecution’s “cartoon of a villain.” (Cohen repeatedly harped on Bankman-Fried’s allegedly good-faith actions throughout his address to the jury.)

[sources/Is_Sam_Bankman-Fried_a_bad_man_or_a_good_boy_Lawyers_swap_opening_statements_before_first_witnesses_take_the_stand]
- Prosecutors alleged Bankman-Fried stole customer funds to finance his lifestyle, political donations, and risky bets through Alameda Research.
- Defense attorneys argued Bankman-Fried acted in good faith, built successful businesses, and did not defraud anyone.
- Witnesses include a victim who lost nearly $100,000, a former friend who admitted to unwittingly writing criminal code, and upcoming star witness Gary Wang.
- The trial highlights the debate over whether Bankman-Fried was a 'man' who lied or a 'boy' who made mistakes in a high-risk startup environment.
- Key figures like Caroline Ellison, Damian Williams, and venture capital partners are expected to provide further insight into the alleged scheme.

[entities/ftx]
- From [[sources/Sam_Altman_backs_teens_startup_Google_unveils_the_Pixel_8_and_TikTok_tests_an_ad-free_tier]]: A cryptocurrency exchange that collapsed, leading to the trial of Sam Bankman-Fried.
- From [[sources/Is_Sam_Bankman-Fried_a_bad_man_or_a_good_boy_Lawyers_swap_opening_statements_before_first_witnesses_take_the_stand]]: A crypto exchange where Sam Bankman-Fried served as CEO.

[sources/Is_Sam_Bankman-Fried_a_bad_man_or_a_good_boy_Lawyers_swap_opening_statements_before_first_witnesses_take_the_stand]
- Sam Bankman-Fried was the former CEO of FTX.
- The trial took place on the second day with lawyers swapping opening statements.
- Thane Rehn is a prosecutor for the government.
- Mark Cohen is one of Bankman-Fried's lawyers.
- Caroline Ellison is the former CEO of Alameda Research.
- Damian Williams is the U.S. attorney for the Southern District of New York.
- Bankman-Fried's parents are his professorial parents.
- Tom Brady and Larry David are celebrities mentioned in the prosecution's account.
- Alameda Research is a crypto hedge fund owned by Bankman-Fried.
- FTX is a crypto exchange where Bankman-Fried was CEO.
- Marc-Antoine Julliard is a Paris-born cocoa trader who lives in London.
- Julliard tried to pull out almost $100,000 on Nov. 8.
- Adam Yedidia is a fast-talking graduate of MIT.
- Yedidia worked at Jane Street before joining Alameda and FTX.
- Jane Street is a high-frequency trading firm.
- Matt Huang is a former partner at Sequoia Capital.
- Gary Wang is a key Bankman-Fried lieutenant.
- Bankman-Fried spent about seven weeks in a Brooklyn prison.
- The trial was held in New York.
- Court adjourned at 4:30 p.m. on the day of testimony.

[entities/alameda-research]
- From [[sources/Is_Sam_Bankman-Fried_a_bad_man_or_a_good_boy_Lawyers_swap_opening_statements_before_first_witnesses_take_the_stand]]: A crypto hedge fund owned by Sam Bankman-Fried.

[raw:sources/Is_Sam_Bankman-Fried_a_bad_man_or_a_good_boy_Lawyers_swap_opening_statements_before_first_witnesses_take_the_stand]
The key to his alleged scheme? Alameda Research, a crypto hedge fund he also owned, argued Rehn. Using Caroline Ellison, his on-again off-again girlfriend and the CEO of Alameda, as a front, Bankman-Fried had “secret access” to customer money—both cash and crypto—the government claimed.

[concepts/customer-funds]
- From [[sources/Is_Sam_Bankman-Fried_a_bad_man_or_a_good_boy_Lawyers_swap_opening_statements_before_first_witnesses_take_the_stand]]: The money belonging to FTX users that was allegedly misappropriated.

[raw:sources/Is_Sam_Bankman-Fried_a_bad_man_or_a_good_boy_Lawyers_swap_opening_statements_before_first_witnesses_take_the_stand]
That answer ultimately lies with the jury, which was selected on Wednesday morning before lawyers for the government and then Bankman-Fried swapped two very different stories of the former crypto mogul’s sudden rise and almost instantaneous fall.

[raw:sources/Sam_Altman_backs_teens_startup_Google_unveils_the_Pixel_8_and_TikTok_tests_an_ad-free_tier]
SBF allegedly tried to buy off Trump: The TC team’s been trained on the Manhattan Federal Court for the trial of Sam Bankman-Fried, the disgraced entrepreneur accused of orchestrating the collapse of cryptocurrency exchange FTX. But fascinating details about SBF’s political dealings are emerging from a book by Michael Lewis, “Going Infinite,” that debuted on the first day of the trial, like SBF’s attempt to buy off Trump to get him to not run again for president.

[raw:sources/Sam_Altman_backs_teens_startup_Google_unveils_the_Pixel_8_and_TikTok_tests_an_ad-free_tier]
Inside the SBF trial: Rebecca and Jacquelyn report on the second day of the SBF and FTX trial. [sources/Is_Sam_Bankman-Fried_a_bad_man_or_a_good_boy_Lawyers_swap_opening_statements_before_first_witnesses_take_the_stand]
The second day of the Sam Bankman-Fried trial featured starkly contrasting opening statements where prosecutors painted him as a liar who stole billions for a lavish lifestyle, while his defense argued he was a good-faith startup founder who acted innovatively and was willing to make customers whole. The proceedings included testimony from a victim, a former friend who admitted to writing code contributing to a crime, and the upcoming appearance of key witnesses like Gary Wang and Matt Huang, setting the stage for the jury to determine the nature of Bankman-Fried's actions.

[sources/Is_Sam_Bankman-Fried_a_bad_man_or_a_good_boy_Lawyers_swap_opening_statements_before_first_witnesses_take_the_stand]
- Prosecutors alleged Bankman-Fried stole customer funds to finance his lifestyle, political donations, and risky bets through Alameda Research.
- Defense attorneys argued Bankman-Fried acted in good faith, built successful businesses, and did not defraud anyone.
- Witnesses include a victim who lost nearly $100,000, a former friend who admitted to unwittingly writing criminal code, and upcoming star witness Gary Wang.
- The trial highlights the debate over whether Bankman-Fried was a 'man' who lied or a 'boy' who made mistakes in a high-risk startup environment.
- Key figures like Caroline Ellison, Damian Williams, and venture capital partners are expected to provide further insight into the alleged scheme.
